## Resources and meanings

All aspects are optional and partial. A name-only subject is a complete minimal
example. When supplied, an authored aspect declares `version: "1.0.0"`.
Registry IDs have major suffix `-v1`; incompatible revisions need new IDs. No
default facts are inserted. Independent local files and installed defaults use
the same loader. Custom profiles/aspects register without changing core code.

| Aspect | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| authored:identity-v1 | Explicit design revision and author attribution; never an individual, run, participant, account or authority |
| authored:lore-v1 | Selected authored context, tags, context links, eligibility, priority, insertion and character budget; private notes excluded from public export |
| authored:guidance-v1 | Model independent instructions and labelled examples; explicit format-adapter requirement, no model catalog or executable templates |
| authored:prepared-v1 | Finite states, input labels, conjunctive equality conditions, offered variants, local media and deliberate generative exits; no forced resident behavior |
| authored:presentation-v1 | App-owned layout and palette vocabulary with text alternatives; no CSS, HTML, scripts or influence over trusted app controls |
| authored:media-v1 | Required/optional asset references, purpose, alternative, attribution and licence; asset metadata does not establish byte availability |
| authored:evidence-v1 | Authored seeds, source-labelled reports and derived text with explicit source, subject, individual/run/participant attribution, audience and narrower derivation |

The existing core identity/dossier/communication/voice, contexts, relationship
subjects and expressions remain available. Typed registry links close dependencies
through the existing bundle selector. Unknown aspects with undeclared semantics
cannot promise semantic dependency closure; only registered links are followed.

Evidence separates design from an asserted source individual, run and participant.
Seeds have no firsthand event authority; reports cite a source-qualified occurrence.
`reported` records an explicit source assertion, not verified truth; `synthetic-report`
additionally labels fabricated fixture material. Both require the same attribution.
Derived material retains source entries and cannot widen audience. This initial
profile refuses firsthand, authenticated-identity and runtime-authority assertions.
It validates explicit claim structure and supported standing, not real authors,
historical truth, cognition, licensing title or cryptographic authenticity. Hashes
only establish bytes. Arbitrary prose is not a semantic truth or secret detector.

Media `license` is a declared rights string (1–8192 characters, nonblank, no
nontext control characters). It carries SPDX identifiers such as `CC-BY-4.0`,
SPDX expressions, or user-declared custom terms such as `LicenseRef-My-Art: ...`.
There is no network lookup, SPDX catalogue certification or ownership authentication.
The author is responsible for the declaration and permission to distribute the bytes;
receivers decide whether those terms permit their intended use. Committed example
resources remain honestly original CC0 material.

## Bounds, privacy and support

Authored entry points bound metadata to 1 MiB UTF-8, 256 records per collection,
64 aspects per subject, 128 entries/states/variants per aspect, 8192 characters per
prose field and 4096 characters of proposed lore context. Core depth64/100000 JSON
values guards still apply. Inline assets are at most 64 KiB each and 256 KiB total;
external assets at most 1 MiB each and 4 MiB total. Limits apply before byte readers.
No network, remote schema, code evaluation, accessor invocation or storage write.
Definition JSON must be one complete standalone value before the duplicate-key-aware
reader processes it; sibling/trailing values and wrapper breakout are refused.

Public export rejects known private paths/claims and private audience labels;
private exchange retains them. Explicit redaction requires a separate selected
document. Audience labels express intent; receiver authorization/filtering before
retrieval/provider projection and temporary persistence remain receiver duties.
Every lore/report audience must be nonempty; public export requires exclusively
`public`. Unknown optional meanings and opaque extensions can travel privately;
public export refuses them until the author selects content with loaded semantics.
Registration establishes declared paths, not universal privacy or secret detection.
Only registered typed links establish dependency closure; opaque payloads cannot
promise that undeclared references or private information were discovered.

Validation distinguishes invalid data, unknown optional transport, required unknown
refusal, incompatible known versions, missing required bytes, metadata-only assets
and verified bytes. A required profile/aspect unsupported by a receiver refuses
before returning a projection. Optional unsupported aspects are named omissions.
Required assets block preparation if bytes are missing; optional missing assets
are named omissions. Admission readiness is never inferred from valid transport.

Validation traverses used profile inheritance and all declared protected aspects,
including absent values, and refuses incompatible protected definitions on actual
import. Receiver consumption compares the full accepted T15 definition snapshot
(schema, links, scopes and privacy included), rather than trusting a version label.
An optional incompatible consumed meaning remains in a validated private view under
an inert alias: IDs, values, scopes, claims and reference graph remain intact while
the old projector cannot consume that meaning. Required incompatible meanings refuse
before any view or callback. The original transport and registry remain unchanged.

Prepared variables have unique keys and nonempty unique values. Conditions use
declared key/value pairs with one condition per key; states and variants have unique
IDs and resolving local transitions. Input names are authored eligibility labels,
never runtime observations or authority; offered exits do not execute a provider.
Evidence `design` names its containing local subject, not a receiver designId.
`source` qualifies the asserted occurrence; neither is global event identity or
proof of history. Individual/run/participant attribution is also an unverified
source assertion. Derivations retain links, reject cycles/duplicates and may only
narrow source audiences. Data transport never admits receiving memory or cognition.

## Receiving purposes

PLC's current plain preset projection stays `{id,name,prompt}` and T465 stays
independent. Rich source data are retained in the package, not secretly appended to
a system prompt. Sonalon uses explicit `sonalon:design-metadata` designId/version
and its other authored sections; missing psychology/history stays missing. Both
receivers own validation, creation/copy IDs, storage and runtime. Create is a
fresh-design candidate; archive copy, selected reports, attachment and continuation
refuse here until separately supported. No generated voice/portrait quality,
browser admission, live resident or rich UI delivery is claimed.

Delivered artifacts: definitions JSON/runtime snapshot, pure validator/receiver report,
three content sources, actual inline bundles, original CC0 resource bytes, fixed
per-target receiving fixtures, standalone and pinned owner-helper tests, README,
mapping matrix and exact-commit contract request. Actual final review scope and limits
are in the ledger: PLC independent receiving-domain review is not PLC implementation
acceptance, and T465 numerical bounds remain provisional compatibility guidance.
Root independently verifies publication before closure; T412 reviews are prerequisites,
not T415 reviews. No human approval gate or runtime/public release follows here.
